statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 12% (low), Stress 36% (moderate), Confidence 87% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC band spanning the U.S. cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks; that band is published as the danger window instead of the whole session. A lighter second checkpoint sits at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and Barkin remarks, and a third in the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping. The reading would change on observed persistent one-way structure: shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near session extremes, or aligned yields, VIX, oil, breadth and megacaps.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures sit mid-range and little changed after the overnight dip was bought back and the session high was rejected; subdued volatility, easing yields and a fifth lower oil session keep tail risk low into the U.S. open
body: Monday closed with the Nasdaq-100 cash index at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83% inside a 29,933.22-30,557.33 day range, as an AI and semiconductor rally lifted the Nasdaq Composite about 2.3% to a record and the S&P 500 about 1.5%. Leadership was narrow: AMD hit an all-time high above $610 and a $1 trillion market value, Intel gained about 12%, Arm about 10%, Meta 11.3% to $741.25 on the reception of its Muse app, and the PHLX semiconductor index rose more than 3%. Overnight the NQ Dec-26 contract fell to 30,670.00, recovered the whole give-back, was turned away from 30,916.50 and now trades near 30,795, up 0.03% against a 30,784.75 prior settlement. Two independent quote sources agree on that level. Price sitting in the middle of the overnight range after both extremes were rejected is direct evidence that retracement is functioning in both directions, which is the main reason Tail stays at 12 while the index sits at a record. VIX at 14.83, down 0.27% in a 14.64-14.95 range, confirms the absence of a volatility bid. Crude has now fallen for a fifth consecutive session to its lowest level in more than two weeks, WTI near 90.13 (-2.42%) and Brent 98.33 (-2.00%), on reporting that Iran could restore Strait of Hormuz shipping if U.S. military pressure eases, that Trump is open to meeting Iran's president at the UN General Assembly, and that Saudi loadings and Hormuz transit volumes are recovering. That diplomacy is unresolved and two-sided, so it is scored as a Stress and headline channel rather than as directional evidence. Rates have eased rather than tightened: the 10-year yield is near 4.94%, about 2bp lower, and the 2-year near 4.74%, which is why Stress slips to 36 in the moderate band. Shared delayed cross-asset context shows megacaps modestly higher on the latest session, 6 of 8 positive with a mean near +0.30%, against semiconductors 5 of 7 lower with a mean near -0.19%, plus soft semiconductor-equipment and firm software readings; that mild rotation away from Monday's chip leadership is a consolidation signal and specifically not the aligned one-way confirmation that would justify a higher Tail. The Finviz futures and calendar sections were unavailable in the latest collection, so futures-level cross-asset alignment could not be checked from that feed; Confidence is nonetheless 87 because the live price, volatility, yield, oil and calendar evidence was obtained and cross-checked directly. Today's scheduled catalysts are the 13:30 UTC cash open, the Richmond Fed manufacturing survey at 14:00 UTC, Williams at 14:05 UTC and Vice Chair Jefferson at 14:20 UTC, then the 2-year note auction and Barkin at 17:00 UTC; Wednesday brings the high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC. None of those has printed, so their importance is carried as conditional Stress rather than as observed structure. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window published as the concentrated conditional band.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments. Tail built steadily through Monday's U.S. session as the index trended to a record close, peaking at 33 with Stress at 57 in the 19:00 UTC hour, which mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES from 14:00 through 19:00 UTC. After the cash close the trend-up characterisation gave way to a normal, two-way regime: Tail fell to 23 by 20:00 UTC and to 14 by 21:00 UTC, then held an 11-13 band through the entire Asian and European overnight, with Stress between 32 and 39 and Confidence between 85 and 87. Every hour from 21:00 UTC onward mapped to EA_ON. Nothing in that sequence has been revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside a 10-18 band, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk is front-loaded into the 13:30-15:00 UTC band covering the cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks, where Tail peaks at 18 and Stress at 48. Lighter secondary checkpoints follow at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction with Barkin, and in the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour. From the 20:00 UTC cash close the path assumes liquidity drains and Tail decays to a 10-11 overnight floor, then rebuilds to 13 late in the window as Wednesday's high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC come into view. Confidence decays from 87 to 61 across the horizon because every hour beyond the current one rests on assumed rather than observed price path.
